desc:
You have n different numbers in nums and you want to line up exactly k of them in a row. Return every possible row. Two rows are different if they differ in at least one position, so [1,2] and [2,1] are both listed.

Rows may be returned in any order.

nums = [1,2,3], k = 2  ->  [[1,2],[1,3],[2,1],[2,3],[3,1],[3,2]]
nums = [7],     k = 1  ->  [[7]]
constraints: -100 ≤ nums[i] ≤ 100 and all values are different
The number of rows n! / (n - k)! is at most 5,040
hints: If k equals n this is the classic task of listing all orderings. Think about what changes when you stop early.
Fill the row from the left. At each slot try every number that is not already in the row.
Stop recursing as soon as the row has k numbers and store a copy of it. Mark numbers used while they are in the row and free them again when you step back.
editorial: Use a recursive search over positions of the row. Keep a used flag per index of nums and the current row. If the row already has k numbers, save a copy and return. Otherwise try each unused index, append its value, recurse, and undo.

The search tree has depth k and each node at depth d has n - d children, so the number of leaves is exactly n!/(n-k)! and every leaf is an answer; nothing is wasted. Time is O(k · n!/(n-k)!) including copying the rows.
solution:
def orderedSelections(nums, k):
    n = len(nums)
    res = []
    cur = []
    used = [False] * n

    def go():
        if len(cur) == k:
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        for i in range(n):
            if used[i]:
                continue
            used[i] = True
            cur.append(nums[i])
            go()
            cur.pop()
            used[i] = False

    go()
    return res
